## Programming Lecture {#sec-02-programming}

### Simulating a random process: coin flips

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
flips <- sample(c("H", "T"), size = 10000, replace = TRUE)
table(flips) / length(flips)
```

### The Monty Hall problem, by simulation

```{r}
monty_hall <- function(switch = TRUE) {
  doors <- 1:3
  car <- sample(doors, 1)
  pick <- sample(doors, 1)
  reveal <- sample(setdiff(doors, c(car, pick)), 1)
  final <- if (switch) setdiff(doors, c(pick, reveal)) else pick
  final == car
}

set.seed(2026)
n <- 5000
p_switch <- mean(replicate(n, monty_hall(switch = TRUE)))
p_stay <- mean(replicate(n, monty_hall(switch = FALSE)))
data.frame(strategy = c("switch", "stay"), win_rate = c(p_switch, p_stay))
```

### Combinations: the birthday problem

```{r}
birthday_prob <- function(n_people) 1 - exp(lchoose(365, n_people) + lfactorial(n_people) - n_people * log(365))
sapply(c(10, 23, 50), birthday_prob)
```

### Distributions: PMF, CDF, and the normal curve

```{r}
x <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 200)
plot(x, dnorm(x), type = "l", lwd = 2,
     main = "Standard normal density", ylab = "density")
```

```{r}
pnorm(1.96) - pnorm(-1.96) # probability mass within ~2 SD
```
